tasks.title: Hand-authored RED oracle for readiness(): all-pass plus one case per failing precondition naming the exact missing artifact
acceptance_criteria: Committed test module ngv2/tests/test_submission_readiness_gate.py contains exactly one all-pass case asserting {"ready": True, "missing": None}.

Contains one failing-precondition case per gate (confidence, live_test, novelty, bounty_eligibility, report_package), each degrading only that single precondition and asserting ready==False with the exact named missing artifact.
Each negative case asserts the precise 'missing' string, never merely ready==False, so a gate that returns a generic/wrong artifact name fails.
All fixtures are built from ngv2.contracts and ngv2_submission_package_builder; the oracle performs no network, subprocess, LLM, wall-clock, or randomness.
The authored tests FAIL against the module's declared mutant and PASS against the correct implementation (non-vacuous RED oracle).

spec.objective: Ship a hand-authored, non-vacuous RED oracle that pins the readiness() contract: exactly one fully-grounded all-pass admission and one case per failing precondition, each asserting the exact named missing artifact so no precondition can be silently weakened or collapsed into a generic failure.
functional_requirements: All-pass case: a fully-grounded package (confidence in {CONFIRMED,HIGH}, live-tested verdict 'confirmed', novelty 'NOVEL', bounty GO with target_spec, readiness_score==3) asserts readiness(...) == {"ready": True, "missing": None}.
Confidence case: only confidence degraded (e.g. 'MEDIUM') asserts ready==False and missing=='confidence'.
Live-test case: only live_report degraded (verdict not 'confirmed' or not live-tested) asserts ready==False and missing=='live_test'.
Novelty case: only novelty degraded (e.g. 'POSSIBLE_DUP'/'CONFIRMED_DUP') asserts ready==False and missing=='novelty'.
Bounty case: only bounty degraded (decision not 'GO' or target_spec None) asserts ready==False and missing=='bounty_eligibility'.
Report-package case: only package degraded (readiness_score<3) asserts ready==False and missing=='report_package'.

Oracle hygiene: fixtures constructed solely from ngv2.contracts and ngv2_submission_package_builder, no network/subprocess/LLM/wall-clock/randomness, and each assertion checks the exact 'missing' value rather than truthiness.
spec.interfaces: Tests import ngv2.submission_readiness_gate.readiness and exercise it with fixtures from ngv2.contracts (Finding/PoC/LiveTestReport, VERDICTS) and ngv2_submission_package_builder (build_submission_package / readiness_score). Asserts the {"ready", "missing"} contract.
edge_cases: Each negative case degrades exactly one precondition so it cannot be masked by an earlier-precedence failure.
Live-test negative covers both a non-confirmed verdict and the not-live-tested flag to bind both halves of that precondition.
Bounty negative covers both a non-GO decision and a GO-with-null-target_spec to bind both halves.
Report-package negative uses a real package whose readiness_score is 2 (one artifact short) rather than a hand-faked score.
non_goals: Do not test the package builder, confidence, or novelty gates themselves (only consume their outputs as fixtures).
Do not test human approval, submission, or FSM wiring.
Do not assert on internal helpers or precedence beyond what the public readiness() contract guarantees for single-failure cases.
spec.implementation_notes: Reference the module's missing-artifact vocabulary constants where exposed so the oracle stays in lockstep with the implementation. Keep one assertion per case on the full returned dict (or on both keys) to maximize mutation sensitivity. Ensure the suite is RED against the declared mutant of ngv2.submission_readiness_gate — e.g. a mutant that returns a generic missing name or flips a comparison must be caught by the exact-string assertions.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: One fully-grounded baseline fixture (CONFIRMED confidence, live-tested 'confirmed' report, 'NOVEL', bounty GO+target_spec, package readiness_score==3) and five single-precondition-degraded variants derived from it. VERDICTS from ngv2.contracts and real packages from ngv2_submission_package_builder scoring 2 and 3.

token_budget_ratio.note: Test-authoring task: no production code; all budget is the hand-authored RED oracle.

tasks.title: Pure readiness() gate (report -> awaiting_submission) admitting only fully-grounded packages
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/submission_readiness_gate.py exposes readiness(finding, poc, live_report, novelty: str, bounty: dict, package: dict, confidence: str) -> dict returning exactly {"ready": bool, "missing": str|None}.

ready==True with missing==None iff ALL hold: confidence in {CONFIRMED,HIGH}; live_report is live-tested with verdict=='confirmed'; novelty=='NOVEL'; bounty-eligible target; readiness_score(package)==3.

When any precondition fails, ready==False and missing names EXACTLY the one failing artifact from the fixed vocabulary {confidence, live_test, novelty, bounty_eligibility, report_package} — never a generic failure and never None.
Function is deterministic and total: no exception on malformed/missing inputs, and a fixed precedence order resolves multi-failure inputs to a single named artifact.

Module imports only Python stdlib and ngv2.* (ngv2.contracts VERDICTS, ngv2_submission_package_builder.readiness_score); no network, subprocess, LLM, wall-clock, or randomness; does not perform approval/submission and does not wire any FSM transition.
tasks.verification_command: python -c "import ngv2.submission_readiness_gate as g; assert g.readiness(None,None,None,'POSSIBLE_DUP',{},{}, 'LOW')=={'ready': False, 'missing': 'confidence'}"

spec.objective: Implement a pure, stdlib+ngv2-only readiness gate that admits a finding package to the human only when every grounding precondition holds, and otherwise halts naming exactly the single missing artifact, porting the BEHAVIOR of the legacy services/mcp_server.py submit_finding gates (dedup/novelty, bounty-eligibility, live-tested, readiness) without computing any of those signals itself.
functional_requirements: Expose readiness(finding, poc, live_report, novelty: str, bounty: dict, package: dict, confidence: str) -> dict whose value is always a dict with exactly the keys 'ready' (bool) and 'missing' (str|None); pure with no side effects.
Return {"ready": True, "missing": None} if and only if all five preconditions hold simultaneously.
Confidence precondition: when confidence is not in {"CONFIRMED","HIGH"}, return {"ready": False, "missing": "confidence"}.

Live-tested PoC precondition: when live_report is absent, not live-tested, or its verdict is not 'confirmed' (verdict validated against ngv2.contracts VERDICTS), return {"ready": False, "missing": "live_test"}.
Novelty precondition: when novelty is not exactly 'NOVEL', return {"ready": False, "missing": "novelty"}.

Bounty-eligibility precondition: when the bounty dict does not indicate an eligible/qualified target (decision=='GO' with a non-null target_spec), return {"ready": False, "missing": "bounty_eligibility"}.
Report-completeness precondition: when readiness_score(package) (consumed from ngv2_submission_package_builder) is not exactly 3, return {"ready": False, "missing": "report_package"}.

Determinism & totality: resolve any combination of failing preconditions to a single missing artifact via the fixed precedence order [confidence, live_test, novelty, bounty_eligibility, report_package], and never raise on malformed, None, or wrong-typed inputs.
spec.interfaces: readiness(finding, poc, live_report, novelty: str, bounty: dict, package: dict, confidence: str) -> dict == {"ready": bool, "missing": str|None}. Consumes ngv2.contracts (Finding/PoC/LiveTestReport, VERDICTS) and ngv2_submission_package_builder.readiness_score(package: dict) -> int. Upstream signals (compute_confidence, classify_novelty, qualify, build_submission_package) are passed in as already-computed arguments, never invoked here.
edge_cases: All preconditions fail at once -> missing == 'confidence' (highest precedence) and ready == False.
confidence is lowercase 'high' or 'confirmed' -> treated as not eligible (exact upper-case membership) -> missing == 'confidence'.
live_report present but verdict is a non-confirmed value in VERDICTS (e.g. 'refuted'/'inconclusive') -> missing == 'live_test'.
live_report present but live_tested flag false even with verdict 'confirmed' -> missing == 'live_test'.
bounty decision 'GO' but target_spec is None -> missing == 'bounty_eligibility'; decision 'SKIP'/'UNKNOWN' -> missing == 'bounty_eligibility'.
readiness_score returns 0,1,2 -> missing == 'report_package'; only exactly 3 passes.
None / empty-dict / wrong-typed arguments for any parameter -> no exception, deterministic not-ready result naming the first failing artifact in precedence order.
non_goals: Do not build the submission package or compute its completeness score (consume ngv2_submission_package_builder.readiness_score).
Do not compute confidence or novelty (consume ngv2_grounding_confidence_gate and ngv2_novelty_gate outputs passed as arguments).
Do not perform human approval or any submission (that is ngv2_human_approval_gate).
Do not wire the lifecycle FSM transition (that is ngv2_lifecycle_fsm_wiring).
Do not weaken any precondition or introduce network, subprocess, LLM, wall-clock, or randomness.
spec.implementation_notes:
Evaluate preconditions in the fixed precedence order and return on the first failure so exactly one artifact is named. Define the missing-artifact vocabulary as module-level constants so the RED oracle can reference them. Guard every consumption (live_report attributes, bounty dict access, readiness_score call) with total, exception-free logic — wrap readiness_score in defensive handling so malformed package -> 'report_package' rather than a raised error. Compare confidence and novelty by exact string membership/equality. Keep the module free of any I/O or import beyond stdlib + ngv2.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Fixtures for a fully-grounded package (confidence CONFIRMED/HIGH, live_report live-tested verdict 'confirmed', novelty 'NOVEL', bounty {decision:'GO', target_spec:{...}}, package with readiness_score==3) and single-precondition-degraded variants. Use ngv2.contracts VERDICTS for valid/invalid verdict strings and ngv2_submission_package_builder for real packages scoring 0..3.

token_budget_ratio.note: Compact pure module; the bulk of value is in exhaustive precondition + totality testing, so test budget dominates.
